Macrons

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

increasingly adverb

also more and more, ever more, more every day

classical

Cic. Att. 14.18.4: dē Graeciā cotīdiē magis et magis cōgitō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Phil. 1.5: cum cotīdiē magis magisque perditī hominēs tēctīs ac templīs urbis minārentur (Lewis & Short)

magis magisque (magis et magis)

the adverb magis doubled

more and more, increasingly

Also magis ac magis, and in verse magis magis (Catullus). Often with cotīdiē or in diēs for growth over time.

Other words

  • in diēs (+ comparative) — increasingly, by the day

    phrase: in with the accusative plural, with a comparative or magis · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 25: tantō hic magis in diēs convalēscēbat (Lewis & Short); Liv. 23.18.12: cōnsuētūdine in diēs blandius

    “More by the day”: in diēs blandius, more seductive every day. Without a comparative in diēs is simply “day by day, daily” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • dē Graeciā cotīdiē magis et magis cōgitō

    every day I think more and more about GreeceCic. Att. 14.18.4 (Lewis & Short)

  • malest, Cornificī, tuō Catullō, malest, mē hercule, et labōriōsē, et magis magis in diēs et hōrās

    your Catullus is unwell, Cornificius, unwell, by Hercules, and in pain, and more so every day and hourCatull. 38.1–3

  • somnus enim et vīnum et epulae … balineaque et ōtium cōnsuētūdine in diēs blandius ita ēnervāvērunt corpora animōsque

    for sleep and wine and feasting, baths and idleness, more seductive every day from habit, so weakened their bodies and spiritsLiv. 23.18.12

See also increase, more, little by little.
